note: A naive random-split F1 on this dataset is ~0.996 but is inflated by template leakage (see script docstring). The 5fold_mean number is what should be reported/defended - it's the average across 5 different group-aware splits, not one lucky split. real_holdout is a more conservative additional check using only hand-collected, non-templated data - hyperparameter tuning (C=2.5) improved 5fold_mean by ~3 points but did NOT move real_holdout at all, confirming the gap is a data problem (need more real documents), not a tuning problem.
